departure_point.description_winter: If arriving by car, it is better to start the ski routes at the Fläschloch cable car valley station (P. 931) due to the limited number of parking spaces.
departure_point.public_transport_stop_comment: Unobtrusive point on the road along the east shore of Wägitalersee. That is where the hiking and skiing routes towards Hohfläsch-Hütte, Schiberg or Zindlenspitz begin. Those who travel by public transport: from the bus stop Innerthal, Post, on foot follow the road (ca. 45 min.), rent a bike at Gasthaus Stausee https://www.gasthaus-stausee.ch/ (phone. 055 446 12 79), take a boat taxi https://waegitalersee.ch (phone 055 446 13 44), use http://www.alpentaxi.ch, Mobility from Siebnen Wangen train station or hitch a ride. There are a few parking spaces 500 metres further into the valley at the Fläschloch cable car valley station.

destination_poi.description_summer: Zindlenspitz is one of the most characteristic mountains of Wägital. Viewed from the valley, it looks so uninviting that you hesitate to choose it as your hiking target. However, the steep limestone tooth is astonishingly easy to climb: T3, which does not even qualify the summit as an alpine hiking summit.
destination_poi.description_winter: Mit seinen beiden Nachbarn Rossälplispitz und Brünnelistock gehört der Zindlenspitz zu jenen wenigen Bergen des Wägitals, die ihren Winterschlaf weitgehend ungestört geniessen können. Denn der Abschnitt zwischen Aberliboden und Zindlen ist nur für Freunde steiler und ruppiger Waldwege ein Thema.

segments.description: At P. 931 a signpost points to several possibilities. Follow it to Aberli and take the steep trail to reach Hohfläsch-Hütte (1368 m; mostly open in summer). Continue to the alp buildings at Hohfläschen and, disregarding the bifurcation at P. 1592, continue to Hohfläschenmatt (1687 m).
segments.title: P. 931 – Hohfläschenmatt

segments.description: The next target is the saddle between Brünnelistock and Rossälplispitz. The map shows a path which goes right, traverses the mostly dry Aberlibach, passes P. 1705 on the left and then ascends eastward. However, this faint path is often interrupted. Alternatively, from the buildings continue towards Mürli for a little while and then traverse right at ca. 1800 m. Here the path is slightly more visible, provided you find its beginning. Both variants merge at ca. 1830 m. This point can also be reached pathless. Now ascend eastward on scree to reach the foot of the seemingly compact rock wall. Only from close range an ascending ledge can be seen that overcomes this wall on the right-hand side. Then the path turns around a rocky nose to lead up the grassy terrain to the saddle P. 1989.
segments.title: Hohfläschenmatt – saddle P. 1989

segments.description: To reach Brünnelistock keep right from the saddle to follow a distinct path on the gentle, grassy ridge or slightly on the left. Further up there are a number of rocky sectors. Some are scrambled on the ridge, others are bypassed on the right or the left. Mostly the path is obvious, sometimes variants are possible. Apart from the surefootedness and the scrambling skills (degree I) a head for heights is required, as the ridge is narrow and on the left and right there is a gaping abyss. Finally, Brünnelistock (2132 m) is reached. The descent is on the ascent back to the saddle at P. 1989.
segments.title: Detour to Brünnelistock

segments.description: A good trail, one passage equipped with a long fixed rope, leads up to the summit structure of Rossälplispitz. Continue on easy rocks (fixed rope) to the highest point (2075 m). Descend along the fixed ropes to reach the saddle at P. 1901 on a grassy ridge. Here a marked trail coming from Hohfläschenmatt merges. Continue to follow the ridge and after a few minutes you reach a steep rocky outcrop. It offers good holds and is equipped with a strong chain. At ca. 1990 m the trail traverses the Zindlenspitz east face on a comfortable ledge to reach the ridge at P. 1979.
segments.title: Saddle P. 1989 – Rossälplispitz – P. 1979

segments.description: From P. 1979 zig-zag up, the last stretch on easy, slightly exposed rocks to reach the spacious summit plateau of Zindlenspitz.From the summit descend to P. 1979. Now on a mostly good trail descend westward in pastures to Ober Zindlen and Zindlen (1535 m). Further down the trail enters the steep forest. On a wide, but rather tiresome trail with slippery and instable gravel descend in many serpentines to Aberliboden. On the bridge at P. 1101 go across Ziggenbach, then immediately turn left to reach Aberli and the starting point.
segments.title: P. 1979 – Zindlenspitz – P. 931

teaser: Zindlenspitz on the normal route has a marked mountain hiking trail up to the summit, which does not exceed T3. To make it somewhat more appealing for alpine hikers, we add two more summits, Brünnelistock and Rossälplispitz. This way we get a spectacular and very rewarding ridge hike which is one of the great classics of the region.
teaser_title: Summit triumvirate between Wägital and Glaris
title: Brünnelistock, Rossälplispitz and Zindlenspitz

reference_poi.description_summer: Höchster Punkt der nördlichen Wägitaler Berge, also der Kette um Zindlenspitz, Schiberg, Bockmattli und Chöpfenberg. Auf allen Seiten felsig, schickt er einen Bug ostwärts ins Oberseetal. Unter Alpinwanderern ist der Brünnelistock vor allem als Teil der «Wägitaler Trilogie» bekannt, zusammen mit Rossälplispitz und Zindlenspitz.

Je nach Perspektive versteckt sich der Rossälplispitz hinter dem bekannteren und leicht höheren Zindlenspitz – oder bildet die Mitte des Dreigestirns, noch sekundiert vom Brünnelistock. Das namensgebende Rossalpeli befindet sich in einer Mulde südwestlich des Gipfelaufbaus, während der Berg nach Südosten mit einer weiten und anhaltend steilen Grasflanke – dem «Heuberg» – ins Oberseetal fällt
reference_poi.description_winter: Eher ein Ziel für Winteralpinismus denn für Ski- und Schneeschuhtouren, insbesondere wegen der Felsstufe unterhalb des Rossalpeli.

description.description:
P. 931 – Hohfläschenmatt 2 h 15 min
Hohfläschenmatt – Brünnelistock 1 h 15 min
Brünnelistock – Zindlenspitz 1 h 30 min
Zindlenspitz – P. 931 2 h

Ascending to the saddle at P. 1989, there are a few narrow, slightly exposed ledges without scrambling passages. Then follows the crux of the tour: the stretch from P. 1989 on the ridge to the Brünnelistock summit, which has some exposed passages without belaying possibilities (T5–). On Rossälplispitz there are some fixed ropes; firstly on a not especially exposed passage, secondly on the rocky summit slope (T3+). On the way to Zindlenspitz there is a steep, rocky outcrop with good holds and a robust chain (T4–) plus some easy scrambling passages shortly before the summit. Apart from a short stretch above Hohfläschenmatt (in easy pastures), there are always distinct paths. Do not undertake the tour in wet conditions!
